title: GTA 6: Stop Killing Games Movement Distances Itself from Leaks
description: As an extended look at GTA 6 approaches, the Stop Killing Games movement has firmly distanced itself from recent leaked videos by Cyberleek.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Impending GTA 6 Official Showcase Overshadowed by Leaks

As the gaming community eagerly anticipates the launch of Rockstar Games' blockbuster GTA 6 later this year, anticipation has reached a fever pitch. This week marks the debut of an extended look at GTA 6, providing fans with their very first official glimpse of the game itself ahead of its scheduled release.

Unfortunately, this exciting buildup has been accompanied by a spate of leaked videos emerging online over the past week or so. These unauthorized leaks have been traced back to an individual or group identifying themselves as Cyberleek, stirring considerable debate across various online gaming forums and social media platforms.

## Stop Killing Games Movement Issues Warning

In response to the unauthorized distribution of footage, the Stop Killing Games movement has publicly distanced itself from the leaks. Taking a hardline stance against the copyright infringement, the organization issued a clear warning to the gaming public regarding the source of the leaked material: "Do not send these people your money."

This firm declaration aims to discourage players from supporting or financially backing those responsible for the security breaches, steering the community back toward official channels as the industry prepares for the game's official gameplay debut.

## Editor's Take

Leaks are an unfortunate reality for major titles like GTA 6, but the swift action by the Stop Killing Games movement to distance itself from Cyberleek is a welcome stance. Supporting official developer presentations over illicit leaks helps protect the integrity of the industry we all love.
